# MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated from the trogon-atlas-mcp tool registry. Do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run rust:mcp-reference`. -->

Every tool the `/mcp` endpoint registers, rendered from the tool registry and
its role policy table. A crate test fails when this page is stale or when a
registered tool and its policy row disagree.

- **Minimum role** is the lowest role whose `tools/list` includes the tool.
  It is the highest role the server requires over the listed gRPC methods.
  The server still authorizes every call; the listing never grants access.
- When the server does not advertise the `who_am_i` feature, `tools/list`
  cannot learn the caller's role and lists every tool. When learning the role
  fails, it lists reader tools only.
- **Effect** comes from the tool's annotations: `read`, `write`, or
  `destructive` for writes annotated as able to remove or overwrite data.
- **Profiles** are the tool profiles that offer the tool. A tool in no
  profile is offered only when the session runs without one. See
  [MCP tool profiles](mcp-tool-profiles.md).
- **Parameters** are the top-level input fields. A trailing `?` marks an
  optional field.

| Tool | Minimum role | Effect | Idempotent | Profiles | gRPC methods | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accept_source_snapshot` | writer | destructive | no | `source-integration` | `AcceptSourceSnapshot` | `request_json` | AcceptSourceSnapshot: connected backend source control. Explicit selectors and ownership only. Returned scope, fidelity, incomplete and recovery state remain authoritative; preview is not an apply receipt. |
| `apply_manifests` | writer | write | yes | `authoring`, `repair` | `BatchGetEntities`, `BatchMutate` | `dry_run?`, `manifests_yaml`, `operation_id?` | Apply one or more YAML manifests (same format as trogon-atlas apply): create missing entities, update changed ones, skip unchanged ones, as one atomic batch. Set dry_run to validate without persisting. Non-blocking validation findings, strategic ones included, come back in the `issues` array as {severity, code, subject, field, message, op_index, op_entity} (op_index is the position among the changed manifests sent, op_entity the manifest's entity id): fix every warning and error. Each write is bound to the revision it was planned against: if another writer changed or created an entity in between, nothing is written and the call fails with data.category "stale_state" and data.next_action "replan", naming the entity with expected_etag and actual_etag (null means absent); call again to plan from fresh state. A dry run that sends a batch and has it validated also returns `consequence_delta`: which findings the change would introduce, resolve or leave unknown (advisory, never a refusal). It is absent when every manifest is unchanged (no batch is sent) or when the server could not compute it; an absent delta never means no findings changed. |
| `apply_source_run` | writer | destructive | no | `source-integration` | `ApplySourceRun` | `request_json` | ApplySourceRun: connected backend source control. Explicit selectors and ownership only. Returned scope, fidelity, incomplete and recovery state remain authoritative; preview is not an apply receipt. |
| `batch_get_entities` | reader | read | yes | `authoring`, `repair`, `review`, `source-integration`, `read-only` | `BatchGetEntities` | `refs` | Batch fetch entities by (kind, namespace, slug, version) tuples. Returns the entities in arbitrary order (missing entries omitted). |
| `batch_mutate` | writer | destructive | yes | `repair` | `BatchMutate` | `operation_id?`, `ops`, `validate_only?` | Atomic batch of put/delete operations. Each op specifies op='put' (with entity_b64) or op='delete' (with kind/namespace/slug/version). Failure rolls back the whole batch and is reported as an MCP tool error whose data carries category/next_action (and code/next_action_detail when applicable), never as a success envelope with status=STATUS_FAILED inside it. Non-blocking validation findings, including strategic ones (BoundedContext, Domain, Subdomain rules), come back in the `issues` array next to binpb_base64, each tagged with op_index and op_entity of the put or delete op that produced it (validate_only dry runs included): fix every warning and error; an empty array means none. |
| `batch_mutate_json` | writer | destructive | yes | `repair` | `BatchMutate` | `request_json` | Atomic batch of put/delete operations expressed as a proto3 JSON BatchMutateRequest (no protobuf tooling required). Failure rolls back the whole batch and is reported as an MCP tool error whose data carries category/next_action (and code/next_action_detail when applicable), never as a success envelope with status=STATUS_FAILED inside it. Non-blocking validation findings, including strategic ones (BoundedContext, Domain, Subdomain rules), come back in the `issues` array next to binpb_base64, each tagged with op_index and op_entity of the put or delete op that produced it (validate_only dry runs included): fix every warning and error; an empty array means none. |
| `begin_artifact_upload` | writer | write | no | `authoring`, `repair` | `BeginArtifactUpload` | `request_json` | Request an artifact upload over gRPC with request_json containing namespace, filename, mediaType, size in bytes, and sha256 as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. The response identifies uploadId and expiresUnixSeconds. Only when directUpload is true, use a file-capable HTTP tool to PUT the raw bytes to the direct S3 presigned uploadUrl with the exact returned headers and no Atlas bearer or AWS credentials. When directUpload is false or omitted, no HTTP upload URL is provided: send the bytes through authenticated UploadArtifactContent gRPC using an SDK, or run the Atlas CLI artifacts upload command where the file is accessible. After either transfer succeeds, call complete_artifact_upload with namespace and uploadId. Remote MCP cannot read caller-local file paths. Keep S3 upload URLs transient; persist the completed artifact reference. |

Explicit selectors and ownership only. Returned scope, fidelity, incomplete and recovery state remain authoritative; preview is not an apply receipt. |

Preserve exact original UTF-8 byte ranges, date, exclusions and quoted-use handling. Selected policies and term use periods apply. Prose matching remains separate in check_glossary_usage; findings do not rename software. |

| `merge_branch` | writer | destructive | no | `repair` | `MergeBranch` | `auto_merge?`, `dry_run?`, `json?`, `keep_branch?`, `name`, `operation_id?` | Merge a branch onto baseline (Phase 2: Review and merge). Set dry_run to run full detection and validation without persisting even on success; the result splits the landable entries into added_count, changed_count and deleted_count and lists the post-merge findings, strategic ones included, in validation and, as JSON, in `issues` (Warning and Info findings are non-blocking; fix them). keep_branch controls whether a successful, non-dry-run merge deletes the branch afterward (default: deletes it). Set auto_merge to land the combined result for edit/edit conflicts whose two sides changed different fields. A dry run that reaches validation also returns `consequence_delta`: which findings the change would introduce, resolve or leave unknown (advisory, never a refusal); it is absent when the merge has conflicts or when the server could not compute it, and an absent delta never means no findings changed. Every dry run also returns `change_assessment`: the server's advisory verdict (`land`, `needs_review` or `reject`) with stable reason codes and the snapshot ids, entry etags, scope and catalogue revision it is bound to. A verdict never changes what the merge itself does; assess again if any bound input moves. |

## Task prompts

Each task procedure is an MCP prompt, fetched with `prompts/get` by the
session doing that task, so the server instructions stay short. A session is
offered a prompt only when its profile, and its role when known, offer every
tool the prompt names.

| Prompt | Description | Tools | Profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `generate-glossary` | Extract contextual vocabulary from pinned sources, obtain explicit expert review, retrieve selectively and refresh without losing publication. | `who_am_i`, `inspect_glossary_sources`, `put_entity_json`, `get_glossary_term`, `get_glossary_definition`, `review_glossary_term`, `list_glossary_entries`, `list_glossary_pointers`, `compare_glossaries`, `check_glossary_usage`, `check_glossary_code_usage`, `inspect_glossary_refresh`, `validate_project`, `create_branch`, `diff_branch`, `get_entity_history`, `export_namespace` | `authoring`, `repair` |
| `author-storyboard` | The storyboard authoring rules validation enforces, and the follow-up after each mutation. | `get_entity_json`, `list_entities`, `put_entity_json`, `validate_event_model` | `authoring`, `repair` |
| `design-strategic-layout` | Where bounded contexts, the problem space and their language live, and how contexts relate. | `put_entity_json`, `validate_project` | `authoring`, `repair` |
| `author-specification` | How to record contract artifacts in the native specification entity. | `apply_manifests`, `get_entity_json`, `get_entity_schema`, `put_entity_json` | `authoring`, `repair` |
| `declare-reliability` | How service level indicators, objectives and alert policies point into the model. | `put_entity_json`, `validate_project` | `authoring`, `repair` |
| `repair-validation-finding` | Scope a finding, gather its dependencies, apply a guarded repair and verify it. | `batch_mutate_json`, `delete_entity`, `get_entity_json`, `get_impact`, `get_incoming_references`, `get_outgoing_references`, `list_validation_rules`, `retarget_references`, `validate_event_model`, `validate_project` | `repair` |
